findings.claim: Users who already put `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on their `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class` now get a compile error. The generated partial adds a second `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, and `ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` has `AllowMultiple = false`, so the build fails with CS0579 'Duplicate attribute'. Projects that annotated their resolver manually to get exactly this behaviour stop building. The same template change affects the composite resolver partial.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.UserResolverAlreadyExcludedFromCoverage_CompilesWithoutDuplicateAttribute. It passes on base and fails on head with CS0579.

findings.claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Consumers compiling for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework therefore get no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` on any generated formatter or resolver. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on .NET Framework 4.0+ and netstandard2.0 and allows `AttributeTargets.Class`, so the guard is not needed for compilation. It leaves the requirement ('all generated code decorated') unmet for a large share of consumers, such as libraries targeting netstandard2.0.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.ResolverExcludedFromCoverage_WhenCompilingForNetStandard20. It drives the generator with the NETSTANDARD2_0 preprocessor symbol and asserts the resolver symbol carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute; it fails on head.
